raw_response:
I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband is gone now, and my son works in Shijiazhuang. He comes back for the big harvests, but the daily work is mine. My knees give me trouble, so I cannot push myself too hard, but I manage.

Everyone around here grows wheat and corn — the land suits it, and I know these crops. I will plant wheat on my 4 mu this autumn, the same 济麦22 improved variety I bought from Zhang's seed shop last year. It did well. I will not try some new type I don't know — at my age I don't need that worry. For corn in summer, I use hybrid seeds,郑单958. Everyone here uses it and the yield is dependable.

For fertilizer, I will put down compound fertilizer when I plant the wheat, then spread urea again in spring when the plants green up. My neighbor uses a little less, but I give a bit more to feel safe about the yield. For corn, my son comes in July and helps me apply urea — it is too heavy for me alone.

I will water the wheat three times: before it goes into winter dormancy, again in spring, and once when the grain is filling. The village canal still works. Corn needs water twice — once when it is young if there is no rain, and again around tasseling.

After wheat harvest in June, I clean up the stubble with the rotary tiller and plant corn right away. No time to waste.
